notes:
Lead origin: inbound demo request via blog post on ticket summarization (Mar 2).
Product: lightweight automation layer that sits on top of Zendesk/Gmail -> triage, auto-summarize, and optionally call tools to update ticket state.
Why Redwood: looking for predictable latency and a hosted API to keep initial ops simple. Interested in tool-calling to trigger ticket state changes and structured JSON output for downstream systems.
Key ask from demo: streaming responses for real-time agent assist, structured output schema support (ticket_summary, priority, suggested_tags), and inexpensive token costs.

Budget: small monthly spend to start (proof-of-value), potential expansion if POC shows 30-40% agent time savings.
Decision-maker: Head of Product (Emily Ramos) + CTO (Mark Liu) for procurement sign-off.
Other notes: prefers self-serve sign-up to test hosted endpoints first; will run a 2-week POC with sample traffic (est 3–8 rps).

use_case_summary: SMB support automation: ingest Zendesk tickets -> generate concise summaries, extract structured fields (issue_type, priority, customer_sentiment), and optionally call ticketing APIs to tag/close tickets. Emphasis on lightweight hosted API, low onboarding friction, and clear cost visibility.
additional_context: Team is engineering-led, plans to self-serve for initial testing. Would rather avoid Dedicated/Private in phase 1. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations after POC if unit cost is high.
pain_points: High agent MTTR on simple tickets; manual tagging inconsistent; current ML experiments are too costly and unreliable at scale.
preferred_success_criteria: POC shows >=30% reduction in agent handling time, structured outputs reach >95% parsing reliability, and per-ticket cost under $0.10 for summaries at P95 latency.
